source.title: A path-norm toolkit for modern networks: consequences, promises and challenges
source.authors: Antoine Gonon; Nicolas Brisebarre; E. Riccietti; Rémi Gribonval

record.tranche_reason: The authors evaluate how path-norm bounds compare with observed generalization on ImageNet ResNets and report the bounds are far too large for dense models; sparsity reduces the path-norm while retaining strong accuracy. This refines the scope and practical usefulness of path-norm-based generalization measures.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, random-label, sharpness, or memorized-example claims. Its own ResNet18 ImageNet experiments report path-norm and accuracy outcomes under pruning; cited prior correlation results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates path-norm bounds and pruning on ImageNet ResNets, which test none of V1–V8. Path-norm is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Random-label fitting and previous generalization-measure correlations are discussed through cited work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The toolkit extends path-norm analysis to modern networks, but its evaluated bound is approximately 30 orders of magnitude too large for dense ResNet18 on ImageNet. Pruning reduces the path-norm substantially while retaining useful accuracy; obtaining informative bounds alongside good performance remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a general path-norm toolkit and evaluates its bounds and path-norm values on pretrained and sparsified ResNets; it does not reproduce the listed studies' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning iteration changes the reported path-norm and test top-1 accuracy; the text reports the first 11 iterations and iteration 19 separately.

fits_no_version.finding: Iterative magnitude pruning with rewinding reduces ResNet18's L1 path-norm from approximately 10^30 to 10^17. Test accuracy exceeds the dense model for the first 11 iterations and remains far above chance after 19 iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning can substantially reduce L1 path-norm while retaining useful ImageNet classification performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The evaluated dense ResNet18 path-norm bound is approximately 30 orders of magnitude too large to explain observed generalization; no margin choice makes the corresponding classification bound informative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The evaluated L1 path-norm bounds are uninformative for standard pretrained ImageNet ResNets.

record.problems: The sparse-network results are from a single run. The authors note that the theorem's data setup does not strictly match their experiment: training uses augmentation, while the bound is evaluated using inference-normalized images; they ignore this mismatch. Several plotted trajectories have no exact numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 also plots path-norms and train/test accuracy across epochs and pruning iterations, but those trajectories are figure-only without textual numeric summaries. No additional rows were reconstructed from the plot.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting paired with natural-label and random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions, including interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T5 is inappropriate relative to these versions: challenging path-norm bounds does not challenge V7's sharpness correlation. The pruning experiment uses one run, and the authors acknowledge that augmentation prevents their experimental setup from strictly satisfying Theorem 3.1.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning or weight-decay conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps; the paper measures path-norm instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured L1 path-norm for the dense ImageNet model before pruning.
rows.note: The paper reports this value as the dense-network starting point for the pruning comparison.
rows.check: The value is supported, but it measures no listed version. Distinguish the dense model trained for the pruning experiment from the PyTorch pretrained ResNet18 in Table 3; the latter has L1 path-norm 1.3 × 10^30.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained with iterative magnitude pruning plus rewinding
rows.operation_detail: Measured L1 path-norm after 19 pruning iterations.
rows.note: The authors summarize this as a decrease of up to 13 orders of magnitude.
rows.check: The reported decrease to approximately 10^17 is supported, but path-norm under weight pruning measures no listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained with iterative magnitude pruning plus rewinding
rows.operation_detail: Compared test top-1 accuracy of pruned models with the dense model.
rows.value: better than with the dense network
rows.note: One reported aggregate statement covering the first 11 pruning iterations.
rows.check: The accuracy improvement during the first 11 pruning iterations is supported, but weight pruning tests no listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained with iterative magnitude pruning plus rewinding
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test top-1 accuracy after 19 pruning iterations.
rows.value: way better than what would be obtained by guessing at random
rows.note: The text does not give a numeric accuracy for this condition.
rows.check: Accuracy far above random guessing after 19 iterations is supported. Natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence with random-label fitting.
